It is a read-only external directory at C:/tmp/AI-Qadam-Events-Bot-Spec/ containing README.md, PRD.md (the requirements — scope, data model, state machines, functional requirements FR-1..FR-17, invariants, acceptance criteria, build order), USER-STORIES.md (42 stories as 3C cards), STORY-DETAILS.md (per-story preconditions, flows, edge cases), RE-EVALUATION.md, DESIGN-REVIEW.md, JOURNEY-AUDIT.md. source_text.spec-owner: Viktor Drukker, v3, dated 2026-08-04. PRD's closing rule: 'if a requirement is ambiguous or contradicts reality, stop and ask. Do not invent business rules — especially around capacity, consent, and who may see personal data.' In this humanless pipeline, 'stop and ask' resolves to core-directives.md's Zero Manual Work clause 1: record the ambiguity and its options explicitly in the requirement's description, or as a decisions/ draft — never silently pick one.

task.description:
Adapt the AI Qadam Events Bot specification into registered requirements in docs/agents/requirements.yaml, per WF-01 Step 1.

DECIDED CONTEXT — read docs/agents/decisions/0003-events-bot-subproject.md first and treat it as settled (a decisions/ record is never overridden, per core-directives.md's Instruction Precedence). It establishes: (a) the bot is a SUBPROJECT of this repo, not a separate repo; (b) the repo becomes a monorepo with apps/web (the existing Next.js site, MOVED from the repo root) and apps/bot (new); (c) the bot is TypeScript/Node on Postgres. Do not re-litigate any of these three, and do not draft a requirement that contradicts them.

WHAT TO DRAFT. Start ids at REQ-007 (REQ-001a..REQ-006 exist and are all done; never reuse or renumber). Cover, in dependency order:

1. THE MONOREPO MIGRATION — moving the existing site from the repo root into apps/web (src/, messages/, public/, next.config.ts, tsconfig.json, eslint.config.mjs, Dockerfile, deploy/, and the CI workflow paths), establishing the workspace root, and creating the apps/bot skeleton. This MUST come first and everything else depends on it. It is a FRONTEND-DEV requirement (it is the site's own files moving) and must be sized to one agent turn — split it if it does not fit. Its acceptance criteria must include that the site still builds, still serves all four locales (ru/uz/en/kk), and that deploy/CI still resolves the moved paths.

2. THE BOT'S RELEASE 1 — PRD §4 and §14 define Release 1 as the Meetup #3 scope (20 stories) and give an explicit build order: skeleton/DB/config/i18n → venues+events CRUD+event card → profile+registration+capacity+waitlist+promotion+withdraw → scheduler (T-24h 'Still coming?', T-3h route+QR) → check-in (MANUAL LIST FIRST, then QR, plus EventStaff and walk-ins) → feedback/NPS. Follow that order in your depends_on chain; the spec states twice that the manual check-in list is built before the QR scanner, and that ordering is a requirement, not a preference.

3. Do NOT draft Release 2 or Release 3 requirements in this run. Registering ~20 more entries that cannot start until Release 1 lands is registry noise. Note in the final requirement's description that Releases 2-3 are a later WF-01 run, and what they cover.

SIZING IS THE HARD PART. WF-01 Step 1.3.c requires each requirement to fit ONE agent turn. 'Registration + capacity + waitlist + auto-promotion + withdraw' is a build-order STEP, not one requirement — split such steps into several depends_on-chained requirements. Expect meaningfully more than one requirement per build-order step. Err toward smaller.

EACH REQUIREMENT MUST: use the exact existing schema (id, title, owner, status: pending, description, acceptance_criteria, depends_on) — do not invent fields; name owner as BACKEND-DEV or FRONTEND-DEV (the new roles exist as of this run — see AGENT_SYSTEM.md §4); cite real paths (apps/bot/..., apps/web/...) and the PRD section/FR number it derives from; carry at least 2 concrete, verifiable acceptance criteria.

THREE THINGS THE SPEC IS EMPHATIC ABOUT — carry them into the requirement text, do not let them evaporate:
- Values that are COMPUTED AND NEVER STORED: no_show, waitlist position, seats taken, registration_open, finished, speaker lineup, past talks. A requirement must not create a column for any of them.
- The PRD §12 invariants and the PRD §10 privacy rules, which this repo has already codified as docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md S1-S14. Where a requirement implicates one, cite the S-number in its acceptance criteria so SECURITY-REVIEWER's Step 2c gate has something concrete to check.
- tg_id is NULLABLE and is never a business key; always resolve to the internal user id.

AMBIGUITIES YOU WILL HIT — record, do not resolve silently: the exact Telegram framework (grammY vs Telegraf) and the ORM/migration tool are explicitly left open by decision 0003; the doors-open time question is open in the spec's README ('Open questions for Viktor'); and this repo has NO TEST FRAMEWORK, which AGENT_SYSTEM.md §7 now flags as imminent because the bot's admission state machine and idempotency rules cannot be verified by a manual checklist. Handle each per Zero Manual Work clause 1 — a named decision to be made inside a specific requirement, or a decisions/ draft — never an invented answer.

Append only. Do not reorder, renumber, or rewrite REQ-001a..REQ-006, whose descriptions cite pre-migration root-relative paths and stand as historical records (decision 0003 says so explicitly).
acceptance_criteria: Every new requirement has id, title, owner, status, description, >=2 concrete acceptance criteria, and depends_on — using the existing schema with no invented fields.
Ids start at REQ-007 and are sequential; REQ-001a..REQ-006 are byte-for-byte unchanged (verifiable by git diff showing only appended lines).
The monorepo migration requirement comes first in the dependency graph and every bot requirement transitively depends on it.
The Release 1 dependency chain follows PRD §14's stated build order, with the manual check-in list preceding the QR scanner.
No requirement creates stored state for a value PRD §5 lists as computed-never-stored.
Every requirement implicating a privacy/authz/token/consent/audit property cites the relevant security-invariants.md S-number in its acceptance criteria.
No orphaned depends_on references; no contradiction with a done requirement or with decisions/0001, 0002, or 0003.
Each of the three named open questions (Telegram framework + ORM, doors-open time, test framework) is recorded explicitly rather than silently answered.
No Release 2 or Release 3 requirement is drafted; the boundary is stated explicitly in the final requirement's description.

result.summary: Drafted 26 new requirements REQ-007..REQ-032 into docs/agents/requirements.yaml, append-only (git diff: 1164 insertions, 0 deletions on that file; REQ-001a..REQ-006 byte-for-byte unchanged). Coverage: the monorepo migration (REQ-007 file move + npm workspace root, REQ-008 Dockerfile/deploy/CI repoint, REQ-009 apps/bot skeleton), then PRD 4's Release 1 (Meetup #3) in PRD 14's stated build order across REQ-010..REQ-032. Release 2 and Release 3 deliberately NOT drafted; the boundary and their contents are stated in REQ-032's description. Dependency graph verified acyclic, no orphaned depends_on, and every requirement REQ-008..REQ-032 transitively depends on REQ-007 (verified by script). Build-order chain: REQ-007 -> 008/009 -> 010 -> 011 -> 012 -> 013 -> 014 -> 015 -> 016 -> {017, 018} -> 019 -> 020 -> 021 -> 022 -> 023 -> 024 -> 025 -> 026 -> 027 -> 028 (manual check-in list) -> 029 (QR scanner) -> 030 -> 031 -> 032. PRD 14's 'manual check-in list before the QR scanner' rule is honoured structurally: REQ-029 depends_on REQ-028. Owners are FRONTEND-DEV (007, 008), DATA-DESIGNER (010, 011) and BACKEND-DEV (all others). Every requirement carries >=2 concrete acceptance criteria; criteria touching a privacy/authz/token/consent/audit property cite the specific security-invariants.md S-number (S1-S14 used across REQ-009..REQ-031). No requirement creates stored state for a PRD 5 computed-never-stored value; several carry explicit grep-and-find-zero criteria forbidding exactly those columns.

issues.summary: Telegram framework (grammY vs Telegraf) and the ORM/migration tool are left open by decisions/0003. Recorded as a named deliverable of REQ-009, which requires a docs/agents/decisions/ record per option with a written rationale against PRD 11's constraints. REQ-009's acceptance criteria fail the requirement if a record names only one option. Not silently resolved here.

Test framework: AGENT_SYSTEM.md 7 names this trigger as imminent because the admission state machine, capacity atomicity and notification idempotency cannot be verified by a manual checklist. Recorded as the third decision record REQ-009 must produce, and REQ-009 must make `npm test` runnable at the repo root. REQ-020's and REQ-023's concurrency criteria explicitly depend on that runner existing.

Doors-open time: the spec README's 'Open questions for Viktor' notes the brochure says 19:30 doors / 20:00 start while the reminder quotes the start only. REQ-026's description names both candidate behaviours, implements (a) quote Event.starts_at only because that is PRD FR-7's literal text, and records that (b) would require inventing an Event field the PRD does not define, which PRD's closing rule forbids. A product-owner answer makes (b) a small follow-up requirement, not a rework.

STORY-DETAILS C4 says the manual check-in list is 'Built alongside C3, never after it' while PRD 14 and the spec README both say 'before the QR scanner'. Recorded in REQ-028's description. Resolved toward PRD.md as authoritative per the spec README's own stated reading order; the two agree on substance (the manual list must not trail the scanner) and no behaviour depends on the difference.

Two pieces of user-facing copy the spec assigns to the product owner have no human in this pipeline: the personal-data consent wording and version (USER-STORIES B1: 'needs Viktor's wording and a version number') and the blame-free no-show wording (USER-STORIES D3: 'Viktor should write it'). REQ-014 and REQ-032 each direct the implementing agent to use plain factual placeholder text with an explicit version identifier and to record in its own handoff result that the copy is provisional — not to invent legal-sounding terms.

Two PRD obligations are split across requirements so that each fits one agent turn, with the gap named in the earlier requirement so it is visible rather than dropped: (1) REQ-016 implements the published->cancelled transition but PRD 6's 'cancelling notifies every non-withdrawn registrant' lands in REQ-027, because the send-once ledger does not exist until REQ-025; (2) REQ-023's auto-promotion guarantees at-most-once via an in-transaction send-marker that REQ-025's ledger then replaces, and REQ-025's description states the migration path.

Release 2 (7 stories) and Release 3 (15 stories) were not drafted, per the task's instruction. REQ-032's description enumerates exactly what each covers, with their PRD FR numbers and USER-STORIES ids, and states that PRD 4's 'Later' and 'Non-goals' lists are never to be drafted at all. That is the pointer a later WF-01 run picks up.
